examples: The soil is moist after the rain.
The cake is moist and soft.
A frog has moist skin.
Keep the seeds in moist soil until they sprout.
The dog's nose was cool and moist.
Moist air from the ocean brought fog.
My mom makes soup.
Mom hugged me.
I help my mom.

more.def: A word used for a mother, in everyday talk.
examples: My mom drives me to soccer practice on Tuesdays.
Her mom is a teacher at the high school.
Mom, may I have a snack?
Wait a moment.
It took a moment.
Just one moment!

more.def: A very short period of time, or a particular point in time.
examples: Wait a moment while I find my shoes.
At that moment, the lights went out.
The best moment of the trip was seeing the whale.
We have art on Monday.
See you on Monday!
Monday is when school starts again.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Sunday and before Tuesday.
examples: On Monday, our class is going on a trip to the farm.
The library is closed on Monday.
Many people go back to work on Monday morning.

easy.def: Coins and paper you use to pay for things.
examples: I have money for a toy.
She saved her money.
Dad has no more money.

more.def: Coins and paper bills that people use to buy things or to pay for work.
examples: He saved his money for months to buy a new bike.
The class raised money for the animal shelter.
People use money to pay for food, clothes, and homes.
A year has twelve months.
It is a new month.
I turn six next month.

more.def: One of the twelve parts of a year, such as May or June.
examples: June is the first month of summer.
My grandparents visit once a month.
It rained almost every day this month.
I want more milk.
She has more toys.
Can I have more?

more.def: A greater number or amount of something, or an extra amount.
examples: There are more stars in the sky than anyone can count.
Add a little more water to the paint.
We need two more players to start the game.

easy.def: The first part of the day.
examples: I wake up in the morning.
Good morning!
Birds sing in the morning.

more.def: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.
examples: The farmer feeds the chickens first thing in the morning.
Dew shone on the grass in the bright morning sun.
We have math class on Monday morning.

easy.def: A woman who has a child.
examples: My mother is kind.
Her mother is a nurse.
I help my mother.

more.def: A woman who has a child, or a female parent.
examples: My mother reads to me before bed.
The mother duck led her ducklings across the road.
He made a card for his mother on her birthday.
There is snow on top of the mountain.
We drove up the mountain.
A goat lives on the mountain.

more.def: A very high area of land, much taller than a hill.
examples: It took the climbers three days to reach the top of the mountain.
The mountain was hidden in clouds.
A cold stream runs down the side of the mountain.

easy.def: The part of your face you eat with.
examples: Open your mouth.
The baby put the toy in her mouth.
My mouth is full.

more.def: The opening in the face that is used for eating and speaking.
examples: Open your mouth wide and say ahh.
The hippo opened its huge mouth.
She covered her mouth when she yawned.

easy.def: The place where a river ends.
examples: The ship sailed to the mouth of the river.
A town sits at the mouth of the river.
Birds gather at the river's mouth.

more.def: The place where a river flows into the sea or a lake.
examples: A city grew at the mouth of the river.
Many fish live at the mouth of the river.
We walked to the mouth of the stream.

easy.def: To go from one place to another.
examples: Do not move.
The snail moves slowly.
She moved her chair.

more.def: To change position or place, or to make something change its position.
examples: The clouds move across the sky in the wind.
Please move your bag so I can sit down.
The dancers moved in time with the music.

easy.def: To go live in a new home.
examples: We move next week.
They moved to a new town.
She moved away.

more.def: To leave your home and go to live in a new place.
examples: My family moved to a new town last summer.
They are moving to a bigger house near the park.
Our neighbors moved away, and new ones came.

easy.def: A story you watch on a screen.
examples: We watched a movie.
The movie was funny.
I like movies about animals.

more.def: A story told with moving pictures and sound, shown in a theater or on a screen.
examples: We saw a movie about dinosaurs at the theater.
The movie was long, so we took a break to eat popcorn.
Many movies are made from favorite books.
